excerpt: Setting up Google Business Profile is the single highest-ROI marketing task a local business can do — and it takes about 15 minutes. Here's the complete setup, plus how to turn your profile into a 5-star review machine.

content.text: If you run a local business and haven't finished **setting up Google Business Profile**, you're invisible at the exact moment customers are ready to buy. When someone searches "café near me" or "best salon in town," Google doesn't show websites first — it shows Business Profiles. This guide walks you through the complete setup, verification, and the step almost everyone skips: turning your profile into a steady stream of 5-star reviews.
Why your Google Business Profile matters more than your website

Here's an uncomfortable truth: most customers will never visit your website. They'll find **my Google Business Profile** listing (yours), glance at your star rating, scan two or three reviews, and make a decision in under 30 seconds. Your profile is your storefront window on the internet's busiest street.
Businesses with complete profiles and a healthy stack of recent reviews win the click. Businesses without them watch customers walk next door — literally.
Setting up Google Business Profile, step by step
The actual process of setting up Google Business Profile is refreshingly simple:

items: Go to business.google.com and sign in with the Google account you want to own the listing
Enter your exact business name — no keyword stuffing, Google suspends listings for that
Choose your primary category carefully (it heavily influences which searches you appear in)
Add your address, or mark yourself as a service-area business if customers don't visit you
Add your phone number and website
Verify — usually by postcard, phone, or video verification

content.text: Once verified, complete every single field. Profiles with photos, opening hours, and a filled-out description rank measurably better. Think of **my business page** on Google as a second homepage — because for most customers, it's the only one they'll ever see.
Google Business Profile management: the 10-minute weekly habit
Setup is day one. **Google Business Profile management** is every week after that. The businesses that dominate local search treat their profile like a living thing:

items: Respond to every review — good and bad — within 48 hours
Upload fresh photos monthly (profiles with recent photos get significantly more direction requests)
Post updates, offers, and news to keep the listing active
Keep hours religiously accurate, especially holidays

content.text: The step everyone skips: Google Business Profile reviews

Here's where most guides on setting up Google Business Profile stop — and where the real money is. **Google Business Profile reviews** are the single biggest factor in whether a searcher chooses you or your competitor. A profile with 8 reviews loses to a competitor with 80 reviews almost every time, even if your service is better.

The problem isn't that customers don't want to review you. It's friction: they promise to "[google rate my business](/blog/google-rate-my-business)" later, walk out, and forget within minutes. The fix is removing every step between a happy customer and the review form.

That's exactly why we built our [social media review stands](/#shop): the customer taps the stand with their phone (or scans the QR code) while they're still at your counter, and your Google review page opens instantly. No searching for your business name, no apps, no forgetting. Businesses using tap-to-review stands typically see review volume multiply within the first month.
Don't stop at Google

The same moment of customer happiness that produces a review can also produce a follower. Once your Google profile is humming, point the same tap at your Instagram, TikTok, or Facebook page — we've written a full companion guide on [ways to increase followers on social media for your business](/blog/increase-followers-social-media-business) that pairs perfectly with this one.
Your action plan for today

items: Finish setting up Google Business Profile if you haven't (15 minutes)
Fill in every field and add 10 quality photos
Put a review collection system on your counter — not a hope, a system
Reply to your 5 most recent reviews today
Set a weekly 10-minute calendar reminder for profile management

content.text: Your next 50 customers are searching right now. Make sure what they find is a complete profile, a wall of recent 5-star reviews, and a business that clearly cares.

excerpt: Posting more content isn't the only way to grow. Here are 7 proven ways to increase followers on social media for my business — including the counter-top trick that converts real customers into followers on autopilot.

content.text: Every small business owner has Googled "ways to increase followers on social media for my business" at least once — usually after posting consistently for weeks and watching the follower count barely move. The advice you find is always the same: post more, use hashtags, make Reels. It works, but it's slow. Here are 7 ways that actually move the needle — including one that grows your accounts while you're busy running your business.
1. Convert the customers already standing in front of you

The most overlooked of all ways to increase followers on social media: your physical customers. They already like you — they just bought from you. The only reason they don't follow you is friction. Nobody types your handle into Instagram while holding a coffee.

Remove the friction and the math changes completely. Our [social media review stands](/#shop) let a customer tap their phone on your counter stand and land directly on your Instagram, TikTok, or Facebook page — one tap, follow button right there. It's the closest thing to **auto followers for small business** that actually involves real humans who've been in your store.
2. Make your Google profile feed your socials

Your Google Business Profile and your social accounts should feed each other. Customers who find you on Google are high-intent — give them a reason to follow. (If your profile isn't set up yet, start with our guide on [setting up Google Business Profile](/blog/setting-up-google-business-profile) first — it's the foundation everything else sits on.)
3. Post proof, not promotions

Accounts that grow fastest share customer proof: reviews, before-and-afters, tagged photos, behind-the-scenes moments. People follow businesses that feel alive, not businesses that feel like billboards. Getting more social media followers is a side effect of looking follow-worthy.
4. Put your handle where hands already go

Receipts, table tents, packaging, mirror decals, the counter itself. Every physical touchpoint is a follower opportunity. A QR code or NFC tap at the exact spot where customers wait — that's prime real estate most businesses leave empty.
5. Run a simple follow-back loop

Follow local businesses, suppliers, and regular customers from your business account, and engage with their posts genuinely. Local networks are tight — visibility in your town's comment sections converts to follows faster than any hashtag strategy.
6. Turn every review into content

Screenshot your best Google reviews and post them. It fills your content calendar, builds trust, and reminds happy customers you exist on social. Businesses doing this report getting more social media followers without posting more often — just posting smarter.

Too few reviews to screenshot? Read our guide on the phrase customers actually search — [google rate my business](/blog/google-rate-my-business) — and why they can't find your review page without help.
7. Systemize it so it happens without you

Willpower-based marketing dies by February. The businesses that win at social put systems in place: a stand on the counter, a QR on the receipt, a weekly repost of the best review. When the system runs itself, growth compounds while you sleep.
The bottom line

The best ways to increase followers on social media for my business — and yours — aren't about gaming algorithms. They're about catching people at the moment they already love you, and making the follow effortless. Start with your counter. It might be the highest-converting social media real estate you own.

excerpt: Thousands of people search 'google rate my business' every day — yet your happy customers still can't find where to leave you a review. Here's the fix, from finding your review link to removing friction entirely.

content.text: Every day, thousands of people type **google rate my business** into a search bar. Half of them are business owners checking their own ratings. The other half are something far more valuable: customers actively trying to leave a review — and failing. If your customers have to search to find your review page, you're losing reviews you already earned.
What "google rate my business" searches really tell you

Think about what has to happen for someone to search **google rate my business** on behalf of your business: they had a great experience, they decided to reward you for it, and they opened Google to do it. That is peak customer goodwill. And most of it evaporates within two minutes, because the path from "I want to review them" to a posted review is absurdly long.
Why customers never find your review page

Here's the journey you force on a happy customer today: open Google, spell your business name correctly, pick your listing from three similar ones, scroll down, find the reviews section, tap "write a review." Every step loses people. By step four, most have put their phone away and told themselves they'll do it later. Later never comes.

Customers who want to **write a google review on a business** shouldn't need detective skills. And before you ask — no, they can't just look at **my google reviews history** on their own account and find you there either; that only shows reviews they've already written.
How to get your direct Google review link
Google gives every business a short link that opens the review box directly. Getting it takes two minutes:

items: Sign in to your Google Business Profile at business.google.com
Search for your own business name on Google while signed in
In the management panel, find "Ask for reviews" or "Get more reviews"
Copy the short link (it looks like g.page/r/...)
Test it in an incognito window — the review box should open immediately

content.text: If you haven't claimed your listing yet, our guide on [setting up Google Business Profile](/blog/setting-up-google-business-profile) walks you through it in about 15 minutes. Everything in this article depends on that foundation.
From a link to zero friction

A link in an email footer helps a little. But the real unlock is putting that link physically where your happiest customers already are: your counter, your tables, your checkout. That's the entire idea behind our [social media review stands](/#shop) — the customer taps the stand with their phone or scans the QR code, and your review box is already open. No searching, no spelling your business name, no "I'll do it when I get home."

The google rate my business problem isn't motivation — your customers have it. It's distance. Remove the distance and reviews stop being something you beg for and start being something that just happens.
Reviews feed everything else

Once reviews flow consistently, they become raw material for the rest of your marketing: screenshots for social posts, proof for your website, trust for new customers. And that same one-tap moment can grow your social accounts too — our companion guide covers [ways to increase followers on social media for your business](/blog/increase-followers-social-media-business) using the exact same stand.
Stop hoping customers will figure out how to google rate my business on their own. Hand them the review box while they're still smiling.
